chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Why Tudie led his own band; the Spikes Brothers and Sunshine records
summary: Tudie wanted his own band at One-Eleven; Reb Spikes ran a music store and booking office, and the 1921 Ory and Mutt records are mentioned.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: One other thing I meant to bring up. Why was it that... I mean, Ram and Tudie had worked together, and Mutt, and they were friends. Why did Tudie have the band two blocks away and didn't play in your band?
Well, for the simple reason that he probably wanted his own band. That's the only thing I can see.
What I was getting at, it wasn't the presence of Mutt Carey that hired George Foster rather than Tudie or anything like that?

Well, when I first came to Los Angeles, Tudie had already had the One-Eleven. All of these bands was playing together. So I don't know the situation when you first come here... I know Reb and...the Spikes Brothers had a music store right at the corner and a booking office.
He's still living here, isn't he -- Reb.
Is he lucid? Can he talk?
I don't know. He was in pretty bad shape, the last I heard.
Was someone interviewing him? He must know a heck of a lot of things.
Oh, he would be the guy, if he could tell you. And you could go in there, and he... He usually had little bookings for different guys.
Because I'm just thinking. Those Sunshine records were made in 1921, I think, with Ory and Mutt and...
Yes. Wasn't there a Norscorum(?) label?
Yeah. I think it was in '21 out here.
But it was funny, because that music... "Ory's Creole Trombone" is pretty... You've heard those records, right, those two...?
